title: Everwell Platform Implementation: Launch Huddle
summary: Kickoff huddle to align on onboarding runbook, networking/VPC requirements, stage vs prod rollout plan, success criteria for a 6-week pilot and security deliverables. Agreement to run a baseline latency/cost benchmark next week and to provision staging credentials.
next_steps: Redwood: share staging runbook + network checklist by 2027-11-04
Everwell: provide CIDR ranges and contact for VPC peering by 2027-11-05
Schedule baseline benchmark (30-45m) w/ SE and DevOps for week of 2027-11-08
action_items: Maya Chen - Send staging runbook PDF and onboarding checklist - 2027-11-04
Liam O'Connor - Prep benchmark harness and sample prompt set - 2027-11-07
Derek Wu - Share VPC/CIDR + egress IPs - 2027-11-05
Elena Ortiz - Confirm required encryption certs and KMS integration points - 2027-11-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: Tue Nov 2, 2027 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Everwell Eng Lead), Sofia Morales (Head of Product), Derek Wu (DevOps), Elena Ortiz (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in. Quick check, audio good?
[00:05] Raj: Yep, good here.
[00:07] Maya: Cool. High level — this is our launch huddle to align on the runbook and next week’s bench. Liam and I will take the technical and logistics items.
[00:18] Liam: Hi all. Thought we'd walk the staging -> pilot -> prod flow, network, and security boxes. We have a 6 week pilot on the table per the SOW, want to lock success metrics.
[00:30] Sofia: For us success is twofold: latency under 300ms p95 for conversational flows and cost per 1k requests below the threshold we scoped — roughly $12 per 1k tokens equivalence, that was the rough ask.
[00:43] Maya: Got it. We'll map the request profile to recommended model variant and batching. Note — in Hosted mode we can hit lower ops time but for production you mentioned private VPC?
[00:53] Raj: Yes, we need private deployment or at minimum VPC peering. PHI-ish data will be trimmed but the legal team prefers traffic inside our VPC.
[01:05] Elena: From security perspective SOC 2 and KMS integration are must-haves. We also need audit logs for every inference request, at least 90 day retention.
[01:17] Liam: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM for key wrapping. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM — we have S3/CloudWatch options. Note, our logs exclude raw prompt by default unless you opt in for full-text retention — that might help privacy requirements.
[01:33] Derek: Quick network items — will you need outbound egress IPs or do you do peering? Our infra team prefers peering but we might open firewall rules temporarily.
[01:43] Maya: For Redwood Private we typically request either VPC peering or a handful of egress IP addresses for firewall whitelisting. We'll send a network checklist.
[01:52] Raj: OK. Timeline wise, how long to get staging up once peering info is provided?
[01:58] Liam: If we have CIDRs and an engineer on your side to accept peering we can provision a staging cluster within 48 hours, then run a smoke test. The bench harness will take a few days to tune.
[02:10] Sofia: About the bench — can you replicate expected concurrent users? Our spike profile hits 60 concurrent conversational sessions at peak.
[02:18] Liam: Yes, we'll configure a workload profile with that concurrency and the expected sequence lengths. We'll also exercise cache warmup and KV caching so the latencies reflect warm-state.
[02:30] Raj: You said KV cache — sorry, is that KV cash?
[02:33] Liam: (laughs) KV cache, yes, apologies — key-value cache for decoder KV to reduce repeated token compute.
[02:40] Elena: For compliance, we need to see the SOC2 report and a pen test summary. Do you have a standard security pack?
[02:47] Maya: Yep, we'll share our security package, SOC2 Type II, data handling policy, and our encryption docs. We'll redact customer names as needed.
[02:56] Derek: Any special ports we'll need to open?
[02:59] Liam: Standard -- 443 outbound for control plane and HTTPS for metrics; if you're using peering it's all internal. We can provide exact CIDR and ports in the checklist.
[03:10] Sofia: Onboard logistics: who will be our day-to-day contact for escalations and runbook questions?
[03:14] Maya: I'll be your AE and primary contact for cadence and contract stuff. Liam is the technical lead/SE; he'll run the benchmarks and help with integration. We also have CSM assigned once you're post-pilot.
[03:25] Raj: Sounds good. A couple of edge cases: we have occasional long context sequences (6k tokens). How will the model behave memory-wise and cost-wise?
[03:35] Liam: For long contexts we recommend a model variant with extended context support and quantization settings. Cost will scale linearly with tokens so we'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark results and recommend KV caching strategies.
[03:47] Elena: Any encryption at rest details? We want to use our KMS and not share keys.
[03:52] Liam: You can bring your own KMS; keys never leave your KMS and we use envelope encryption. I’ll include an HSM note if you need FIPS/HSM-backed keys.
[04:02] Maya: Quick commercial note: pilot pricing remains as discussed in the SOW. Post-pilot we can discuss Dedicated capacity or continue in Private mode — we'll document options.
[04:12] Sofia: Ok. For the pilot scope, propose we restrict to two endpoints: conversational assistant and document Q&A, about 100k tokens per week as a start.
[04:24] Liam: That works. We'll create separate benchmark sets for each endpoint so you can see latency/cost per workload.
[04:32] Raj: What about rollback? If the pilot causes incidents we need a clear rollback plan to the existing system.
[04:38] Maya: We'll include a rollback policy in the runbook — canary route, traffic split 10/90, then rollback on errors above threshold. Liam can set up automatic fallback to your existing API for critical routes.
[04:51] Derek: Regarding logs — can we redact PII at the edge before sending anything to Redwood?
[04:56] Liam: Yes, you can implement client-side redaction or use our proxy filter; both patterns are supported. We'll put sample config in the runbook.
[05:06] Sofia: Who signs off on go/no-go for pilot to prod? Internal stakeholders are product and security; infrastructure ops will validate the network.
[05:16] Elena: Security will approve once we see SOC2 and the KMS integration plan and confirm logging/retention meets policy.
[05:24] Maya: Ok we'll target sending the security pack and runbook by Thursday. Liam will run the benchmark next week.
[05:31] Raj: Any blockers we should know about right now?
[05:34] Derek: Just me getting the CIDR ranges and the peering contact — I'll work that today.
[05:38] Maya: Great. Any other questions?
[05:41] Sofia: One more — do you have a sample SLA for Dedicated mode? We might escalate if pilot looks good.
[05:47] Maya: Yes, we have an SLA doc for Dedicated and Private; I'll attach it.
[05:51] Liam: I'll also note two quick tactical items for the bench: we need sample prompts and a small set of user traces to simulate. If you can export a 3-day trace we'll use it.
[05:59] Raj: We'll export anonymized traces and the sample prompt set by Monday.
[06:05] Maya: Thanks everyone, recap: Maya to send runbook + security pack by Thu 2027-11-04; Liam to prepare benchmark and coordinate for week of 11/8; Derek to share CIDR and peering contact by Fri 11/05; Elena to confirm KMS requirements by 11/06. We'll reconvene after benchmark.
[06:21] Sofia: Thanks, see you all next week.
[06:24] (meeting ends)
